correctness.rationale: I verified the argument uniformly for m≥3. In the link on W of u the u-component has size 1+|T|+|T∩S|. For any specified two a-vertices choose an allowed b_k in a third page. Pair faces containing the two a-vertices by toggling b_k in decreasing face size; any larger competing coface has already been removed and different pairs cannot compete. The survivor is a cone. The other link is symmetric, so attaching both cones to Δ(W) along these contractible links gives contractible Y. Faces carrying both hubs have at most one W vertex; the remaining cover piece is the edge joined with discrete W. The two contractible subcomplexes have intersection K_{2,2m}, giving its suspension by the homotopy pushout of the cofibrations; the cycle rank is 2m−1. Integral Mayer–Vietoris is natural because both subcomplexes are invariant. Orient all intersection edges from U to W: an integral cycle has two opposite rows, each summing to zero, which directly identifies its lattice with I_U⊗I_W equivariantly. The layer swap acts by −1 on I_U and has no fixed W vertices even when combined with a page permutation; this gives the two stated traces. Page invariants in I_W are constant on the a- and b-shores with opposite constants, hence the stated primitive integral invariant. After barycentric subdivision the finite group action has no simplex inversions, so the rational quotient chains are the orbit (coinvariant) chains, with exact coinvariants by averaging. This gives exactly the stated rational quotient Betti number. The m=3,4,5 checks are recorded corroboration only; the uploaded program was inspected but not executed.
residual_risks: No equivariant wedge or integral quotient homology is inferred. The collapse requires a third page; it does not prove the two-page case.

value.rationale: A quadrilateral book is a natural nonchordal graph family, and cutoff three is the first that admits all three-vertex selections but forbids a selected page. The uniform wedge count is exact and the integral action adds content beyond Betti numbers and a rational character alone. The invariant lattice and quotient Betti number are concrete consequences, and the cover explains how a bipartite graph controls this topology.
residual_risks: The finding is about one infinite family and one cutoff, and does not imply a general equivariant decomposition.
